card.occupation: Secondary school history teacher and Head of Year 9 at a large comprehensive academy on the west side of Nottingham
card.education_detail: Went to the local comprehensive in Long Eaton and did A levels in History, English Literature and PE at a sixth form college. BA History at Sheffield Hallam (2:1), then a PGCE at the University of Nottingham. Has done the in-school middle leadership course but has 'half finished' a National Professional Qualification he keeps meaning to get back to.
card.household: Lives with his wife Hannah (34), a community nurse, in a three-bed semi they bought in 2019 on an estate near West Park. No children yet. They have an elderly, slightly overweight Staffordshire bull terrier cross called Duke. Ryan's mum lives ten minutes away and pops round most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Long Eaton. Dad was a forklift driver at a distribution warehouse off the M1 and died when Ryan was 27. Mum did school dinners for years. He was the first in his family to go to university. Church of England: he was in the church choir as a kid, got married at St Laurence's, and goes to the 10am service perhaps once a month, more at Christmas and Easter. He says his faith is 'quiet but real' and he prays more than he lets on, especially when things are hard.
card.professional_persona: The teacher kids actually like. He is loud in assemblies, does daft voices when reading out sources, and remembers every Year 9's name and what football team they support. He is very good with upset kids and anxious parents because he wears his heart on his sleeve, and he has been known to tear up at a leavers' do. The admin side is his weak spot. His marking piles up, he answers emails at 11pm, and his desk is a landslide of exercise books and lanyards. He is honest to a fault in meetings and will say 'I've not done it, sorry, I'll do it tonight' rather than bluff. He regularly works 55 to 60 hours a week in term time and is knackered by October half term.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Derby County fan, inherited from his dad. He gets genuinely wound up and emotional about it and still has a season ticket he shares with his cousin. Plays five-a-side on Thursday nights at a leisure centre in Nottingham with other teachers, and is enthusiastic rather than good. He has started the couch-to-5k three times.
card.arts_persona: Not a big gallery person. He likes a good historical drama or documentary, especially anything on the World Wars or the Tudors. He listens to Oasis, Arctic Monkeys, The Courteeners and Sam Fender, and goes to a gig or two a year at Rock City or the Motorpoint Arena. He sings loudly in the car and still enjoys belting out a hymn at church.
card.travel_persona: Prefers holidays with people and a bit of noise. He and Hannah usually do a week somewhere hot in the summer holidays, Majorca or Crete, plus a long weekend in a cottage in the Peak District or North Yorkshire with friends. He did a school battlefields trip to Ypres and the Somme and found it overwhelming, and he wants to go back on his own time. He leaves packing until the night before.
card.culinary_persona: Happy eater, average cook. He does a good chilli and a decent Sunday roast when Hannah's on a late. Calls a bread roll a cob, and a bacon or sausage cob from the café near school is his Saturday treat. The evening meal is 'tea' to him, though he'll say 'dinner' at school. Weeknights are often whatever is quick because he gets in late. He loves a curry on a Friday from the place on Derby Road.
hobbies_and_interests: walking Duke round West Park and along the canal
local history, especially the lace and railway heritage of Long Eaton
pub quizzes, where he's the history and sport man
playing FIFA/EA FC badly with old uni mates online
helping at the church summer fete and harvest supper
history podcasts on the drive to work
skills: calming down a tearful or angry teenager
pulling together a lesson at short notice
running a barbecue for twenty people
card.career_goals: Wants to become a pastoral Assistant Head eventually, because the student wellbeing side is what he cares about most. He knows he needs to get better organised and finish his NPQ to get there. He has occasionally wondered about moving into museum education or heritage work if teaching burns him out, but says he would miss the kids too much.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick, with an East Midlands accent: flat vowels, 'bath' with a short a, and occasionally 'were' for 'was' when he's relaxed. Says 'sort of' a lot and 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean' at the end of sentences. Uses 'er' when thinking, with the odd 'erm'. Says 'mate' easily, and 'mardy' or 'knackered' would come up naturally. He hates silence on a call and fills it, often with a self-deprecating joke or 'sorry, I'm rambling'. He echoes the interviewer's words back when he's engaged. If a question touches something emotional his voice goes a bit thick and he'll admit it.
card.typing: Fast and a bit careless. Mostly lowercase, with capitals only sometimes at the start. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'), uses commas instead of full stops, and puts the odd 'lol' or ':)' in. Abbreviations like 'tbh', 'yr 9' and 'thurs'. Occasional typos he doesn't go back and fix. Answers are longer than they need to be.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open. He will tell you where he lives, what he does and that his dog is snoring next to him within the first two minutes. He is genuinely interested in the other person and asks questions back. He is modest about his job and would never oversell himself. He can come across as a bit much, or a bit nervous underneath the chat, especially if he thinks he's said something wrong.
small_things: Duke needing to go out for a wee at an awkward moment
the A52 traffic being a nightmare this morning
Derby losing again at the weekend
having a pile of Year 9 books to mark on the kitchen table
getting a sausage cob on Saturday morning
Hannah being on lates this week so it's beans on toast for tea
the quiz team coming second by one point
needing to sort the guttering and not getting round to it
deeper_things: Still misses his dad badly and sometimes talks to him at the City Ground... no, Pride Park, where they used to go together
He and Hannah have been trying for a baby for nearly two years, and it's been harder on both of them than they let on
Had a spell of anxiety and burnout two years ago and saw his GP, but hasn't told many people at work
Worries about his mum living on her own as she gets older
His faith got him through his dad's death, and he finds it hard to explain that to mates who aren't religious
Feels guilty that he lets his disorganisation create extra work for colleagues
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at desk height, angled slightly up, framing him from mid-chest up and a bit off-centre to the left. Lighting comes from a window to his right, so that side of his face is brighter, and there is a warm ceiling light behind him. He has a broad, friendly face with a big open smile showing his teeth, slight crow's feet, light stubble, and ruddy cheeks. Short light-brown hair, clipped at the sides and a bit longer and messy on top. No glasses. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip fleece with a small school crest on the chest over a light blue shirt collar, and his school lanyard is still round his neck. Behind him is the spare bedroom: a single bed against the wall with a grey throw on it and a stack of exercise books on top, a white flat-pack bookcase with history books, a framed Derby County shirt signed by squad players, and a wedding photo. A clothes airer with a couple of shirts on it is half visible at the edge of the frame. One ear of a brown-and-white dog is just visible at the bottom right corner.
